analysis.title: GS Duttenhoefer - Duttenhoefer's Daily 09.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 47bps to 7765 (+13.4% ytd) on solid volumes. ETFs were 32% of the tape, the highest since June.
Semis fell, with SOX down 3% (still +78% ytd). Samsung and TSMC were strong but not enough against very high expectations. An OpenAI revenue headline added to the weakness.
US 10yr yield lower at 5.22%. Brent $103, Gold $4177, Bitcoin $82k.
Fed's Waller said there is flexibility on the timing of additional hikes. Market pricing is around 80% for a hike in Dec26.
Trump said not to attack Iran before the midterms. US and Iran continue indirect negotiations through mediators, and Tehran is reviewing US feedback on Iran's proposed seven-day plan.

OpenAI annualized revenue was about $50bn at end of Sep, below the $70bn run rate in an earlier report. This was cited as the reason for the prior day's Tech/Nasdaq weakness, though some sources point to different calculation methods.
DeepSeek models processed 36.8tn tokens on OpenRouter versus a combined 33.0tn for OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and xAI. This captures only OpenRouter traffic, and token volume is not revenue or users.
A CFO survey on AI found finance teams spend 26% of their time verifying or correcting AI output. 65% of CFOs say their most common frustration is confident answers based on the wrong data.
Waymo closed a $5bn term loan, its first debt financing (PIMCO, Blackstone and others), after a $16bn equity investment earlier this year. It launched in its 15th US city last month.
Finland datacenter announcements add more than 1.8 GW of potential capacity, about 14 TWh of annual electricity demand (~17% of Finland's consumption). Forward power prices are up c.40% ytd.
Anthropic cut the Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price to $0.10 per million tokens, adding to AI inference pricing pressure.

Consumer Experience: spending growth on experiences accelerated from 1% in Q125 to 6% in Q126. GS sees attractive valuations, revisions near inflecting and positioning not crowded. The basket is 40% live entertainment, 20% leisure, 20% hotels, 20% cruises.

Asian equities are now the world's 2nd largest market after the US at $50tn market cap. Tech is about half of index cap and earnings, and earnings are forecast to grow 34% from 2026-2028. GS keeps a constructive view.

Q3 earnings season starts next week with JPM on 13 Oct. Consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27%, with AI infrastructure spending accounting for over 50% of the growth and hyperscaler capex growth of 116%.
Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% in Q3 versus 14% in Q2. Median net profit margin is expected at 14.7% in Q3 versus 15.1% in Q2, with input cost pressures despite contained wage growth.
The global active ETF market has grown to more than $1.7tn in AuM.

sector_views.rationale: Experience spending growth accelerated to 6% in Q126, valuations are attractive, revisions are near inflecting and positioning is not crowded. Higher-income exposure insulates the basket from fuel costs.
GS keeps a constructive view. Earnings are forecast to grow 34% over 2026-2028, led by tech, with themes of AI, power, non-tech compounders and shareholder return.

earnings_insights: Q3 US earnings season starts the week of 13 Oct with JPM on 13 Oct. Consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27% in Q3 (consensus estimate, not yet reported).
AI infrastructure spending accounts for over 50% of expected S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116% (consensus estimates).
Median S&P stock EPS growth is expected at about 9% in Q3 versus 14% in Q2 (consensus estimate for Q3).
Median S&P 500 net profit margin is expected at 14.7% in Q3 versus 15.1% in Q2 (consensus estimate for Q3).
Samsung and TSMC results were strong but the stocks did not rally enough given very high expectations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield moved lower on the day, but remains above 5%.
Market pricing implies a likely further Fed hike, consistent with Waller's comments on additional hikes.
Oil remains elevated, and higher fuel costs have weighed on consumer spending.
Consensus expects strong earnings growth driven largely by AI infrastructure spending.

risk_factors: Very high expectations in semis, where Samsung and TSMC strength did not prevent a SOX decline of 3%.
OpenAI revenue headline (about $50bn annualized versus $70bn earlier report) hit Tech and Nasdaq sentiment.
Further Fed hikes, with Waller expecting additional hikes if data come in as expected and the market pricing about 80% for a December hike.
Higher fuel costs are weighing on consumers and input cost pressures are squeezing S&P 500 profit margins.
Falling AI inference prices, including Anthropic's cache-read cut, add pricing pressure across AI.
Forward power prices in Finland are up c.40% ytd due to datacenter demand.
vol_and_positioning: ETF volumes were 32% of the tape, the highest since June, which GS suggests may reflect macro trading.
GS describes positioning in Consumer Experiences as not overly crowded.
geopolitical: US and Iran are continuing indirect negotiations through mediators. Trump described the talks as productive, and Tehran is reviewing US feedback on Iran's proposed seven-day plan.
Trump said not to attack Iran before the midterms.
